parole.significato: iota; the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek ἰῶτα (iôta), from the same Semitic source as English yodh, namely Proto-Semitic *yad- (“hand”).
From Ancient Greek κρόκος (krókos), of ultimately Semitic origin. Doublet of κουρκουμάς (kourkoumás).

parole.significato: bag (of paper or plastic; for shopping, etc)
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek σάκκος (sákkos, “sack, bag; sackcloth”), most likely from Semitic.
From Byzantine Greek σμαράγδι(ν) (smarágdi(n)), from Koine Greek σμαράγδιον (smarágdion), diminutive of Ancient Greek σμάραγδος (smáragdos), of Semitic origin.
